Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up from demo — quickstart questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team liked the low-latency routing and the fallback behavior. A few follow-up items from our side as we scope the pilot:

1) Quickstart: what does a minimal integration look like? We plan to prototype chat support within our web app and want an estimate of engineering time + sample cURL/SDK calls.
2) Endpoints & envs: can we get a short-lived staging endpoint and a separate production endpoint? Any constraints on creating multiple endpoints during the evaluation?
3) Rate limits & headroom: our initial volume will be bursty (100 qps for 30s bursts, sustained 10 qps). What ratecap should we request for the hosted eval?
4) Deployment mode: we discussed hosted vs dedicated vs VPC. For this pilot, we expect to stay hosted but want guidance on when to recommend dedicated.

Also, can you share your quickstart doc and a ratecap template we can fill with our traffic profile?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short call if that’s easier.

Best,
Aditi Rao
Product Manager, BrightCart

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditi Rao <aditi@brightcart.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — quickstart questions

Hi Aditi — great to meet today and thanks for the clear list. I pulled together the short answers below and attached a lightweight quickstart + ratecap template.

Quick answers (high-level):
- Minimal integration: 1–2 engineer-days to wire basic chat using our SDK (server-side call pattern). I’ve included a sample SDK snippet in the quickstart.
- Endpoints: we can provision a staging endpoint (sandbox) and a production endpoint for the eval. You can create up to 3 sandbox endpoints per account during the pilot; production endpoints are limited but we’ll reserve one for you.
- Rate limits: for pilot, request a hosted eval profile with burst allowance up to 150 qps and sustained 12 qps. This gives headroom for your 100 qps bursts and keeps latency SLOs intact.
- Deployment mode guidance: start hosted for speed. Move to Dedicated when you need predictable throughput with reserved GPUs (typical threshold: sustained 50–100 qps per model or strict compliance requirements), or Private if you require VPC/isolation or on-prem.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Fill the attached ratecap_matrix.xlsx with your expected query shapes (tokens/request, chat vs short-completion), peak windows, and retention needs.
2) I’ll provision a sandbox endpoint and a short-lived prod endpoint for testing once we get the completed matrix.
3) We can schedule a 30-min ops preflight with Sean (cc’d) to discuss network egress, auth, and trace sampling.

Attachments: redwood_quickstart.md (sample SDK + cURL), ratecap_matrix.xlsx (template)

If you prefer a call today, I have 4–5pm ET slots.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
